question: hi im a first year and dont know anyone yet, who should i contact if i want to find clubs or ways to meet people on campus?

body.answer:
That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

The Center for Student Involvement oversees student clubs. Its page says all clubs welcome new members, and joining can help students meet friends. Browse the club listings at [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) or start exploring on Archway at [http://archway.ramapo.edu/](http://archway.ramapo.edu/); you can also download the Archway App from the Apple Store or Google Play. If your interests aren’t represented, inquire with the Center about starting a club. [20] You can contact the Center for Student Involvement for information on getting involved. [18] The Center’s page lists more than 160 clubs and organizations to choose from. [21]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [27]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [28]

Sources: [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/involvement-frequently-asked-questions/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/fun/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The directory lists no title for Cindy R. Jebb [1]. Ramapo’s president page describes her as the College’s president and as a retired U.S. Army Brigadier General, Professor Emerita, and the first woman Dean of the Academic Board at West Point. She became Ramapo’s fifth president on July 6, 2021, after 39 years of military service. [5] Before Ramapo, she served as West Point’s 14th Dean of the Academic Board, overseeing its Academic Program and chairing the Academic Board. [4]

question: who is the best professor for intro to biology? i heard some are way easier

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Faculty profiles that list BIOL 101 Introduction to Biology among the courses they teach:
- Paramjeet Bagga, Professor of Biology, pbagga@ramapo.edu [15]
- Yan Xu, Professor of Biology, yxu@ramapo.edu [16]
A profile lists the courses a professor teaches; it doesn't say who teaches which section this term.

I don’t have verified information about which professor is best or easier. The profiles list courses professors teach, but not who teaches each section this term [15][16].

The Orientation Programs page says the instructor is the best source of help for a student struggling with a course; students can talk with instructors before or after class, visit their office, or email them. It also says an academic advisor can help by appointment or during Student Success–Academic Advisement walk-in hours [26].

**Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [27]

Dissections show a complexity in organisms that is invisible to models and computers. question: Who is the director of the Center for Health and Counseling Services? Also what's the phone number

body.answer:
Which office do you mean: Counseling Center, Health Services?

**Counseling Center**

Relevant Experience: Dr. Green is a New Jersey licensed psychologist with more than 25 years of experience working in university and college counseling centers. She completed her pre-doctoral internship at SUNY-Albany’s Counseling Center. She worked in the counseling centers at Seton Hall University and William Paterson University prior to becoming the Director of the Center for Health and Counseling Services at Ramap… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/judith-green/)

Academic Year Hours: Monday – Friday: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm Summer Hours: Monday – Thursday: 8:00 am – 5:15 pm Closed on Fridays [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/)

**Dean of Students**

Update to Health Services: From: The Dean of Students <deanofstudents@ramapo.edu> Date: Fri, Feb 27, 2026 Subject: Update to Health Services Dear Students: As of Monday, March 2, 2026 and through Tuesday, May 12, 2026, Ramapo College will offer free, telehealth services to all students via Bergen New Bridge Medical Center. Appointments will be available Monday through Sunday \(7 days per week\) from 10:00am to 6:00pm. Many me… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/update-to-health-services-feb2026/)

Supporting the Well-Being of Students: The Center for Student Wellness is a multi-disciplinary team which offers free, confidential mental health counseling, crisis intervention, and health promotion services. The unit is staffed by psychologists, social workers, and professional counselors with bilingual staff who speak Spanish. Counseling Services also has a collaborating psychiatrist and Alcohol and Other Drug Counselors. The contac… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/mental-health-and-well-being-resources-fall-2026/)

Mental Health and Well-Being Resources: Alcohol and Other Drug Counselors and a Health Promotions Specialist. The contact phone number to schedule an appointment with Counseling Services is 201-684-7522. Counseling Services is located in D-216. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of death, dying, or suicide, emergency appointments are available in Counseling Services by calling 201-684-7522, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm.… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/mental-health-and-well-being-resources/)

Yes—there are several options:
- Ramapo Esports (Athletics): open to all students to learn about; exclusive membership is for students who try out for the games provided to become an RCNJ Esports Player. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/espo/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/espo/) [18]
- Ramapo Gamers Club (Student Organization): for casual and competitive players, with gaming community and esports events. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/RCES/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/RCES/) [19]
- Ramapo Girls in Gaming (Student Organization): a safe, free and fun environment for female-presenting people and allies to game. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/gaming/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/gaming/) [17]
- Ramapo Smash Club (Student Organization): Super Smash Brothers and other fighting games. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/SMASH/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/SMASH/) [16]
- Trading Card Game Club (Student Organization): trading card games for new, casual and competitive players. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/trading/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/trading/) [20]
- Geek and Nerd Culture (Student Organization): tabletop RPGs, D&D, Minecraft and board game nights. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/GNCulture/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/GNCulture/) [15]
- Rhythm Game Club (Student Organization): weekly rhythm-game meetings and events. [https://archway.ramapo.edu/rhythm/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/rhythm/) [14]

The club directory also lists Technology Animation Studies Club, which includes Pokémon card and video game battles: [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/technology-animation-studies-club/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/technology-animation-studies-club/) [29]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [59]

21. Regular participants in a class session typically consist of the instructor, students registered for the course, and individuals providing disability accommodations authorized by the Office of Specialized Services.
22. Students who are not registered for the course are not permitted to attend.
23. Students may not bring guests (including other students, friends, family members) without instructor permission.

27. Visitors to the classroom/teaching space must follow all procedures and laws regarding student confidentiality.

28. During the designated meeting time for a course, announcements by students or others from outside the class are only allowed if authorized by the instructor.
29. Students should contact the instructor, in advance and in writing, to request permission to make any such announcements.
30. The instructor’s decision is final.
31. Unless authorized to do so by the instructor or when a matter of significant overall College importance requires interruption (as determined by the President or their designee), students may not interrupt a class to discuss matters unrelated to the course curriculum.
32. Students should communicate with other students about non-academic announcements using the policies designed by the Office of Marketing and Communications.

Yes. The Pre-Med/Pre-Health Club welcomes students interested in medical careers and provides informational meetings, guest speakers, volunteer events, and social gatherings. Email premed@ramapo.edu. [8]
For pre-law, the Law School Prep Club is open to anyone considering law school and offers LSAT materials and group study sessions. Email lawschoolprepclub@ramapo.edu. [7]
The directory also lists the Latinx Pre-Law Society: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/LPLSC/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/LPLSC/). [2]
The Center for Student Involvement is the office for clubs and organizations. [9]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [42]

question: which club is the best one to join for making friends? i dont know anyone

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

There isn’t a published “best” club; choosing one depends on your interests. The college says joining can provide “interesting friends”; all clubs listed are open to all students, and welcome new members, ideas and directions. Explore the club list at [https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/). [5] The directory includes groups whose descriptions specifically mention making friends, building community, or welcoming new members, such as Association of Latinos Moving Ahead, Math Club, Knit and Crochet Club, and International Student Organization. [12][34][45][50] The Center for Student Involvement can help you decide which club to join. Browse the club list and ask the Center for Student Involvement about starting a club if your interests aren’t represented. [5]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [51]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [52]

question: what is CMPS 147 about and how many credits is it

body.answer:
CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I is 4 credits. It introduces problem-solving with computers, including computer systems, ANSI C++ programming, algorithm design, program development, debugging, testing and documentation. Topics include variables, data types, expressions, selection, repetition, functions and arrays. A course fee is required. It has the Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR) attribute. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147)

question: Do I need to take PSYC 101 before I can take abnormal psychology or can I take them at the same time?

body.answer:
You do not need PSYC 101 before PSYC 314 based on the catalog’s published prerequisites: PSYC 314 requires CRWT 102 Critical Reading and Writing II or CRWT 102S Critical Reading and Writing II. Its prerequisites do not list PSYC 101. [3]

PSYC 101 has no published prerequisites. [2] The catalog does not state whether you may take them at the same time. Before registering, review the prerequisite requirements in Web Self Service; course descriptions are found in Web Self Service, Course/Catalog Description. [11]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [25]

Undergraduate Degree Programs An undergraduate degree program consists of the General Education program, a major, and free electives. Students have the option to pursue a minor and/or a second major. General Education: The hallmark of a liberal-arts education, the General Education program must provide students the opportunity to acquire competency in at least communication (both written and oral), reasoning (both scientific and quantitative), critical thinking and analysis, and technology. The General Education curriculum should not exceed 41 credits. Students may double count courses in the General Education curriculum and the major. A single course may not fulfill two separate General Education competencies, and no more than two General Education courses may double count in the General Education curriculum and the major. Students may also double count up to two General Education courses in a minor. Major: A major is required for all undergraduate degrees. A major focuses on a particular discipline or an interdisciplinary area. The major requirements typically constitute approximately half of the degree program, must total at least 40 credits, and may not exceed 64 credits (including concentrations, tracks, and prerequisites that are specific to the major). Programs for which national or specialized accreditation standards necessitate a curriculum exceeding 64 credit hours may petition for an exception. Such exceptions must be limited to the minimum additional credits required to maintain accreditation. The petition must demonstrate that the additional credits are required for compliance, and provide evidence that the program has minimized credit requirements to the greatest extent possible while maintaining accreditation. Exceptions shall be granted upon approval by the appropriate governance bodies (ARC, Faculty Assembly and the Provost’s Office), and shall be reviewed on the accreditor’s cycle. For students with two majors, no more than half the courses can double-count in both majors. All writing-intensive courses required for the second major must be completed as well. Concentration: A concentration is a focused area of study within a major. The following criteria apply: A concentration is typically employed in a major that has distinctive sub-disciplines. Multiple concentrations are possible, but each must follow the 50% rule. That is, no more than half the courses may double count in both concentrations. (For example, if students pursue two concentrations each of which requires five courses, no more than two courses can be shared by/double counted in the two concentrations). While reliance on technology for teaching, learning, research, administrative operations, and communication offers countless benefits, it also exposes the College to a wide range of cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities. question: how many credits do I need for a business minor and what courses count

body.answer:
The catalog lists two minors for “business”: Business Analytics Minor and International Business Minor [5]. It gives no total credit count for either minor [1][2]. Its general minor rule is 16–24 credits, including non-general education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits; courses for the primary or secondary major may count, but no more than half the credits required for the minor [9].

The catalog names Business Analytics and Applied AI Minor requirements as: all of BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS, INFO 224 PRINCIPLES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, INFO 310 BUSINESS ANALYTICS I, and INFO 345 AI FOR BUSINESS: HARNESSING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; plus 2 electives from ECON 310 ECONOMETRICS, INFO 233 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING, INFO 311 BUSINESS ANALYTICS II, INFO 320 TOOLS FOR ANALYTICS AND AI, INFO 332 DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS, INFO 333 DATA VISUALIZATION, INFO 422 DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS, MGMT 373 MANAGEMENT SCIENCE, and MKTG 330 MARKETING RESEARCH [1].

International Business Minor: prerequisites ECON 102 INTRODUCTION TO MACROECONOMICS and IBUS 326 FUNDAMENTALS OF INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS; 1 international foundation course from ECON 323 COMPARATIVE ECONOMIC SYSTEMS, ECON 325 INTERNATIONAL ECONOMICS, FINC 415 MULTINATIONAL FINANCE, IBUS 305 POLITICS OF INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT, IBUS 330 FUNDAMENTALS OF IMPORTING AND EXPORTING, or MKTG 350 INTERNATIONAL MARKETING; 1 geopolitical course from BADM 316 WORLD POLITICAL ECONOMY, IBUS 305 POLITICS OF INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT, IBUS 315 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN JAPAN & KOREA, IBUS 321 CHINA AND OTHER BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS IN ASIA, IBUS 322 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN CHINA, IBUS 335 DOING BUSINESS IN LATIN AMERICA, IBUS 336 DOING BUSINESS IN AFRICA, IBUS 337 IMMERSION COURSE IN PERU, IBUS 340 EUROPEAN BUSINESS COMMUNITY, or POLI 205 COMPARATIVE POLITICS; and 1 additional elective from BADM 316 WORLD POLITICAL ECONOMY, ECON 323 COMPARATIVE ECONOMIC SYSTEMS, FINC 415 MULTINATIONAL FINANCE, IBUS 300 INDEPENDENT STUDY: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS, IBUS 315 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN JAPAN & KOREA, IBUS 321 CHINA AND OTHER BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS IN ASIA, IBUS 322 INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS IMMERSION COURSE IN CHINA, IBUS 330 FUNDAMENTALS OF IMPORTING AND EXPORTING, IBUS 335 DOING BUSINESS IN LATIN AMERICA, IBUS 336 DOING BUSINESS IN AFRICA, IBUS 340 EUROPEAN BUSINESS COMMUNITY, MKTG 350 INTERNATIONAL MARKETING, or POLI 205 COMPARATIVE POLITICS [2].

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [19]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-BAAI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-IBUS) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [19](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

## First-Year Seminar | Overview
82. First-Year Seminar (FYS) is the first course in the general education curriculum of Ramapo College of New Jersey and it serves as the introduction to general education and liberal learning.
83. The goal of FYS is to develop students’ critical thinking skills using open discussion, reading, writing, and experiential learning.
84. FYS courses are open only to first-semester, first-year students and they are designed expressly to acclimate new Ramapo College students to the higher academic expectations they will be asked to meet throughout their years of college study.
85. First-Year Seminar is the home of the Ramapo College Summer Reading Program.
86. All incoming first-year students will be required to read a common book selected by students, faculty, and staff members, which will be used as a discussion topic in the FYS course.
87. Students are expected to read the book during the summer months prior to joining the Ramapo community and they will be asked to discuss issues raised in the reading and to write thoughtful responses to questions that develop in the course of engaging discussions.

## First-Year Seminar | Fall 2026 Courses
88. A total of 44 FYS courses comprise the FYS program in 2026.

## First-Year Seminar | First-Year Seminar Courses
90. Individual First-Year Seminars are based on themes and topics that are as diverse as the instructors who teach them.

98. Seminars have limited class sizes (20 – 25) that allow students and instructors to get to know one another in a comfortable setting.
99. A limited class size allows students to feel welcome and to encourage participation in academic discussions that are the hallmark of seminar courses.
100. Most of the seminars are interdisciplinary: that is, they introduce ideas and ways of thinking from more than one discipline (history and geography, for example, or chemistry and art).
101. Students are encouraged to choose their seminar with topics they find appealing, and to be flexible in their choices.

question: what GPA do I need to make the dean's list and what happens if im on academic probation

body.answer:
To qualify for the Dean’s List, you must be a matriculated undergraduate student, complete a minimum of 12 cumulative credits (not including “P” grades), have no incomplete grades for that semester, attain a semester GPA of at least 3.5, and have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Part-time students taking fewer than 12 credits per semester are not eligible. The list is published at the end of fall and spring semesters. [14]

Undergraduate students with a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for two consecutive semesters are placed on Academic Probation and cannot appeal their standing. Toward the middle of fall and spring semesters, the Provost or designee emails students on probation with a reminder of their standing and actions to take once grades are posted. With a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, a student is placed in good standing after probation. With a semester GPA of at least 2.5 but cumulative GPA still below 2.0, a student previously on probation is placed on Continued Probation for one semester. Students previously on Continued Probation who reach a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 are placed in good standing after probation. [9]

answer:
To qualify for the Dean’s List, you must be a matriculated undergraduate student, complete a minimum of 12 cumulative credits (not including “P” grades), have no incomplete grades for that semester, attain a semester GPA of at least 3.5, and have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Part-time students taking fewer than 12 credits per semester are not eligible. The list is published at the end of fall and spring semesters. [14]

Undergraduate students with a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for two consecutive semesters are placed on Academic Probation and cannot appeal their standing. Toward the middle of fall and spring semesters, the Provost or designee emails students on probation with a reminder of their standing and actions to take once grades are posted. With a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, a student is placed in good standing after probation. With a semester GPA of at least 2.5 but cumulative GPA still below 2.0, a student previously on probation is placed on Continued Probation for one semester. Students previously on Continued Probation who reach a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 are placed in good standing after probation. [9]

question: which is easier, biology or psychology major? I have a 2.8 gpa right now, do you think I can still get into the nursing program

body.answer:
I can't predict that.

I don’t have verified information on which major is easier or whether your 2.8 GPA would get you admitted; the pages give no admissions decision for your circumstances. Admissions says transfer applicants are strongly recommended to have at least a 2.5 GPA; accelerated BSN applicants need 3.0 or above, and Biology applicants need 2.75 or above [5]. First-year applicants to Nursing should meet the criteria: GPA 3.0 or higher, 4 years of math and science courses, and strong grades in math and science; apply directly and submit required documents prior to December 15 [7].

For the generic BSN, complete the listed pre-nursing courses: one of MATH 108 or PSYC 242; all listed science courses (BIOL 212/212L, BIOL 214/214L, BIOL 216/216L, CHEM 111/111L, and PSYC 101). Nursing courses require C+ or better [4]. The ABSN is for applicants with a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally accredited institution. Its six bridge course pairs/courses require C+ or better to proceed, and all listed Nursing courses require C+ or better [3]. ABSN requirements and application instructions: [https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/) and [https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/) [6]. All Ramapo Nursing majors must take the exam [16].

The Center for Student Success helps students choose a major. Talk with faculty in those majors; its page suggests choosing based on interests and strengths [9][11]. First-year and undeclared students are assigned Professional Advisors there, except Nursing, EOF, and Environmental Science students [12].

- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [28]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [28]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/faqs/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/teas-faq/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I can't predict that.

I don’t have verified information on which major is easier or whether your 2.8 GPA would get you admitted; the pages give no admissions decision for your circumstances. Admissions says transfer applicants are strongly recommended to have at least a 2.5 GPA; accelerated BSN applicants need 3.0 or above, and Biology applicants need 2.75 or above [5]. First-year applicants to Nursing should meet the criteria: GPA 3.0 or higher, 4 years of math and science courses, and strong grades in math and science; apply directly and submit required documents prior to December 15 [7].

For the generic BSN, complete the listed pre-nursing courses: one of MATH 108 or PSYC 242; all listed science courses (BIOL 212/212L, BIOL 214/214L, BIOL 216/216L, CHEM 111/111L, and PSYC 101). Nursing courses require C+ or better [4]. The ABSN is for applicants with a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally accredited institution. Its six bridge course pairs/courses require C+ or better to proceed, and all listed Nursing courses require C+ or better [3]. ABSN requirements and application instructions: [https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/) and [https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/) [6]. All Ramapo Nursing majors must take the exam [16].

The Center for Student Success helps students choose a major. Talk with faculty in those majors; its page suggests choosing based on interests and strengths [9][11]. First-year and undeclared students are assigned Professional Advisors there, except Nursing, EOF, and Environmental Science students [12].

question: i have a hold on my account and cant register for spring classes. how do i find out what its for and who do i contact to get it removed

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

To find out what the hold is for and get next steps, contact the Center for Student Success ([https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/)) or the Office of Student Accounts ([https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/)). [17] Student Accounts says the Hold Flag will be removed once your account is paid-in-full. [1]

- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [25]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [25]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/returning-student/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

11. The Room Change Request form is available on Thursday, 11/12/26.

14. Students with approved Room Changes move to new assignments on Spring 2027 Check-in Day, 1/18/27.

27. Prohibited Items: Residents in traditional residence halls, Bischoff Hall, Laurel Hall, Mackin Hall, The Overlook and Pine Hall, are not allowed to have household appliances, as outlined in the prohibited items list (https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/prohibited/).
28. However, residents of The College Park Apartments and The Village may use most household appliances.
29. All students planning to relocate are strongly encouraged to review the prohibited items list (https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/prohibited/)before moving.

32. 33. If no meal plan is selected, residents will automatically be assigned the Tasty 10 meal plan.

39. The Office of Residence Life is conducting an open room change request period for Spring 2027.

41. (https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) Room change request forms are due by November 24, 2026 at 11:59pm.

44. Residents who are approved for a room change must visit their Hall RA Office before moving into their new assignment.

49. If you completed Step Three of the Housing Selection Process and have since decided to withdraw your housing request for Fall housing, please email reslife@ramapo.edu (mailto:reslife@ramapo.edu)for further instructions.

51. Living on campus means being part of a shared community—not just renting a room.

52. What is a Direct Deposit?
53. Direct deposit is also known as Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT).
54. It is the transfer of funds from Ramapo College to an individual student’s checking or savings account at a participating bank, savings and loan association or credit union.
55. Direct deposit delivers your money quickly and safely.
56. The difference is a check isn’t printed or mailed.

76. Anything you usually do with your money now, you can also do with Direct Deposit.
